title: Booking Holdings Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Misses on FTC Charge
excerpt: Adjusted EPS rose 17% to $4.66 and gross bookings climbed 10% to $54.5 billion, but a $900 million FTC-related revenue reduction pushed reported revenue down 1% and fourth-quarter guidance points to slower growth.
body:
• Booking Holdings' third-quarter adjusted earnings rose 17% to $4.66 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.48, while reported revenue fell 1% to $8.89 billion after a $900 million FTC-related revenue reduction.
  • Travel demand held up underneath the charge: room nights grew 7% to 345 million and gross bookings rose 10% to $54.5 billion, and adjusted revenue — excluding the FTC item — increased 9% to $9.8 billion.
  • Adjusted EBITDA increased 9% to $4.61 billion at a 47% margin, and the company repurchased $2.1 billion of stock, with $12.4 billion of authorization remaining.
  • For shareholders: the dividend is $0.42 per share, payable December 31, 2026 to holders of record on December 11 — but fourth-quarter guidance points to slower growth, with room nights up just 1% to 3% and adjusted EBITDA about flat.

Booking Holdings beat Wall Street's profit expectations in the third quarter of 2026 even as a regulatory matter cut into its reported revenue. The Norwalk, Connecticut-based travel company, which owns Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, reported adjusted earnings of $4.66 per share on November 3, up 17% from a year earlier and ahead of the $4.48 Zacks Consensus Estimate. On a GAAP basis, earnings were $3.61 per share, up 7%, and net income slipped 1% to $2.72 billion. Per-share figures reflect April's 25-for-1 stock split.

The gap between the adjusted and reported numbers is one item. Booking recorded a $900 million reduction in revenue and accrued a $100 million loss related to a Federal Trade Commission matter, both excluded from its adjusted results. Reported revenue therefore fell 1% to $8.89 billion and missed the consensus estimate Zacks compiled, while adjusted revenue rose 9% to $9.8 billion. "We are pleased with our third-quarter operating performance, as resilient travel demand and disciplined execution by our teams drove double-digit gross bookings growth, margin expansion, and 17% adjusted earnings per share growth," chief executive Glenn Fogel said in the release.

Demand grew even as reported revenue fell

The underlying booking engine expanded through the quarter. Room nights increased 7% to 345 million, and gross bookings climbed 10% to $54.5 billion, or about 11% in constant currency. Zacks reported room-night growth accelerated from 5% in the second quarter, led by Europe and Asia, and constant-currency average daily rates rose about 3%.

The revenue mix continued shifting toward merchant transactions, where Booking.com collects payment directly. Merchant revenues rose 14% to $7.0 billion, while agency revenues fell 4% to $2.46 billion, according to the company's statements. Advertising and other revenues increased to $332 million. Bookings beyond hotel rooms also grew: Zacks reported flight tickets rose 19% and attraction tickets 24%, alternative-accommodation room nights increased 7% to roughly 37% of Booking.com's room nights, and Connected Trip transactions grew almost 20%.

Costs, cash and capital returns

Total operating expenses fell 1% to $5.48 billion, helped by the absence of a $457 million impairment charge recorded a year earlier and by lower transformation costs. Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $4.61 billion, with the margin steady at 47%.

Cash and cash equivalents stood at $15.81 billion at September 30, down from $17.2 billion at the end of 2025, and long-term debt rose to $18.07 billion. Free cash flow fell 22% to about $1.1 billion as deferred merchant bookings unwound seasonally, though both cash measures were up 2% for the first nine months of the year. Booking returned capital through $2.1 billion of share repurchases in the quarter and declared the $0.42 dividend.

A slower fourth quarter ahead

The outlook is the cautious part of the report. For the fourth quarter, Booking guided room-night growth of 1% to 3%, gross bookings growth of 2% to 4%, adjusted revenue growth of 0% to 2% and adjusted EBITDA about flat year over year. Management said travel demand moderated late in the quarter on softer international trends, and October demand was hit by Middle East travel disruptions, elevated airfares and localized unrest in some European cities; guidance assumes those effects persist through year-end. For the full year, the company still expects high-single-digit growth in gross bookings, adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA, with adjusted earnings per share up in the low-to-mid teens. The next test is whether the slowdown stays within that range when Booking reports in February.
